subject.title: Subagent lifecycle observability + async supervision controls

question: Which core contract should own durable subagent lifecycle receipts and audited cancel/steer/resume supervision: the task ledger, the audit ledger, or a dedicated subagent lifecycle API?
rationale: The remaining work defines persistent state, Gateway protocol, operator permissions, redaction, retention, artifact references, and security audit semantics, so automation should not choose the public contract boundary.

options.title: Extend Existing Ledgers
options.body: Use the task ledger for run summaries, audit ledger for supervision receipts, and artifact APIs for pointers so operators get one coherent lifecycle model instead of a parallel store.

options.title: Create Dedicated Lifecycle API
options.body: Introduce a separate SQLite-backed subagent lifecycle ledger and Gateway API if task and audit records cannot express ordered event receipts and action semantics cleanly.

options.title: Narrow To UI/Channel Slices First
options.body: Defer the durable supervision contract and keep related work in narrower timeline or channel-liveness issues until maintainers are ready to define the security boundary.

recommendation.title: Extend Existing Ledgers
recommendation.body: Use the task ledger for run summaries, audit ledger for supervision receipts, and artifact APIs for pointers so operators get one coherent lifecycle model instead of a parallel store.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across subagent lifecycle, registry, announce, and control code that this decision would reshape.
